summary: Adds the QUALITY-owned contract surface for PR #47's android/tools CLI and MetaVR bridge. contracts/tool-rosters/android.yaml is already at the 15-tool ceiling (8 core + 7 seat; ci/gates/check_desk_integrity.py ROSTER_MAX_TOOLS), so rather than force a breaking swap in that always-on roster, this adds a new pack (contracts/tool-packs/androidtools.yaml, 5 tools, seats: [android]) that bot-03-android loads on demand via desk_app_tools_load, plus the contract-change document contracts/changes/spe-5160-android-roster-companion-v1.yaml (G-4, non-breaking). One incidental fix: ci/tests/test_gates.py asserted a hardcoded pack count ('7 rosters, 3 packs') that the new 4th pack broke; that test file is QUALITY-owned (ci/tests/** in ownership.yaml) so the assertion was updated to '7 rosters, 4 packs' in the same change.

not_touched: contracts/tool-rosters/android.yaml (left at its 15-tool ceiling; see 'schema unclear' note below)
services/desk-gateway/** (bot-01-systems-backend's path; backend strings in the new pack are contract-only, not wired)
ownership.yaml (contracts/tool-packs/** was already owner: bot-06-quality-security, contract_surface: true, with contract_consumers already listing bot-02/03/04; no manifest change needed)

schema_unclear_note: The work order asked to 'Update contracts/tool-rosters/ for Android MetaVR / android.tools commands.' contracts/tool-rosters/android.yaml is already at exactly 15 effective tools (the hard ceiling), so adding any new roster tool there requires retiring an existing one — a scope/priority call (which of desk_play_track_status / desk_play_staged_rollout / desk_play_halt_rollout / desk_artifact_size_delta / desk_lint_baseline_diff / desk_contract_ack / desk_app_tools_load would be displaced) this companion change does not make unilaterally. contracts/tool-packs/ is the mechanism the README already documents for exactly this shape of problem (additive, loaded per ticket, capped at 5, never displacing the always-on roster), so that is what this change uses. Filed honestly rather than blocked on; a human or LEAD can redirect if a direct roster edit (with a chosen tool to retire) is actually wanted instead.
